title: Formal union representation remains a minority and uneven workplace institution
source_unit: CPS employed wage and salary worker annual average, age 16+

denominator.unit: thousand employed wage and salary workers

observations.method: BLS CPS annual-average Table 1; representation includes members and workers whose jobs are covered by a union or employee-association contract.
observations.uncertainty: Survey estimate; 2024 annual-average sampling and classification uncertainty apply. No interval is reproduced in this record.
observations.subgroup: All employed wage and salary workers age 16+; self-employed workers excluded.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal coverage is not the whole of worker power; membership and representation do not directly measure schedule control, appeal ability, autonomy, or exit.

denominator.unit: thousand employed wage and salary workers

observations.method: BLS CPS annual-average Table 1; representation includes members and workers whose jobs are covered by a union or employee-association contract.
observations.uncertainty: BLS reports that 2025 annual estimates exclude October because of the federal government shutdown and are not strictly comparable with other annual averages; no interval is reproduced in this record.
observations.subgroup: All employed wage and salary workers age 16+; self-employed workers excluded.
observations.counterinterpretation: The small one-year rate movement cannot establish a trend in practical bargaining power, and the 2025 collection break limits direct year-over-year interpretation.

boundary: This is a CPS representation-context trend, not a causal union-wage estimate or direct measure of worker autonomy, household security, cultural meaning, collective action, or political response. The retrieval hash covers the committed BLS analysis memo.
